chunks.label: Asking how someone is
chunks.rationale: Opens a catch-up with a friend, neighbour or coworker.
chunks.interference: Kawatta koto (anything new) is not kawatta hito (an odd person).
members: 何か変わったことあった？

chunks.label: Saying how you are
chunks.rationale: Gives a quick, modest answer to how's it going.
chunks.interference: Bochibochi and nantoka yatteru both mean 'getting by'; batabata shiteta means busy, not unwell.

chunks.label: Saying it's good
chunks.rationale: Gives a quick positive verdict, from mild to warm.
chunks.interference: Ii n ja nai? and kirai ja nai sound negative but are positive.

chunks.label: Saying it's not great
chunks.rationale: Says you didn't like something without sounding rude.
chunks.interference: Anmari always needs a negative after it; imaichi doesn't.
members: あんまり好きじゃない
期待してたほどじゃなかった

chunks.label: Asking what they think
chunks.interference: Kansou wa? asks about something they saw or tried; for a view on an issue ask dou omou?

chunks.label: Work and free time
chunks.rationale: Covers what you do for work and for fun.
chunks.interference: Hamatteru is a current craze; suki is a lasting like.

chunks.label: Shows, music and news
chunks.rationale: Opens chats about what people watch and listen to.
chunks.interference: Mita? asks about one thing you saw; miteru? asks about a show you're following.
members: 最近何か面白いの見た？

chunks.label: Food and drink
chunks.rationale: Checks what someone can eat and drink and where they like to go.
chunks.interference: Daijoubu? here means 'can you handle it', not 'are you all right'.
members: お気に入りのお店ある？

chunks.label: Picking a side
chunks.interference: 派 is said ha, not wa, even right after a noun.

chunks.label: Seeing someone again
chunks.rationale: Reacts when you meet someone after a long time.
chunks.interference: Yaseta? is a compliment; futotta? said to someone else is rude.
members: 最近ちょっと太っちゃった
前に言ってた〜、どうなった？

chunks.label: Your life news
chunks.rationale: Shares what has changed since you last met.
chunks.interference: Hisashiburi ni (for the first time in ages) is not hisashiburi (long time no see).

chunks.label: Framing your view
chunks.rationale: Marks an opinion as personal, frank or unsure.
chunks.interference: Watashi teki ni wa and butchake are casual; kojinteki ni wa is safe anywhere.

chunks.label: Degree and surprise
chunks.rationale: Adjusts how strong a description sounds.
chunks.interference: Warito (fairly) and ... no wari ni wa (for a ...) share wari but mean different things.

chunks.label: Impressions and likeness
chunks.rationale: Describes what something seems like or how you pictured it.
chunks.interference: Mitai na at the end is a hedge; before a noun it means 'like'.

chunks.label: Comparing things
chunks.rationale: Compares two things and says how much they differ.
chunks.interference: Niteru (looks alike) is always the -te iru form, never plain niru.

chunks.label: It depends
chunks.rationale: Avoids sweeping answers and allows for differences.
chunks.interference: Ni yoru (it depends on) and ni yotte (varying by) are the same verb in two forms.

chunks.label: Matters of taste
chunks.rationale: Talks about likes that split people.
chunks.interference: Suki na hito wa suki da yo ne usually means you are not one of those fans.
members: 好きな人は好きだよね

chunks.label: Responding to a view
chunks.rationale: Acknowledges someone's view without fully agreeing.
chunks.interference: Iitai koto wa wakaru agrees only with the point, and a kedo usually follows.
members: 言いたいことは分かる
そういう考え方もあるね

chunks.label: Pushing back gently
chunks.rationale: Disagrees or criticises without sounding harsh.
chunks.interference: Dou ka to omou looks like a question but states doubt.
members: 偏見かもしれないけど
